I just moved to Lyon 3, and with two cats at home, I called this vet to find out how to register with a vet closer to my home. The man I spoke to on the phone was incredibly unpleasant, arrogant, and unprofessional. When I tried to explain my cat's condition and the medication he'd been taking for years, he kept interrupting me, practically accusing me of lying because, according to him, it wasn't the right medication for my cat's problem and he couldn't understand why anyone would have prescribed it. Fine, I'm not a vet, but there's a reason I go to professionals. He was very eager to end the call because his landline was ringing right after, so he quickly cut our conversation short.
I think there are better ways to speak to prospective clients. Personally, I won't be going to him. I spoke to another vet right after who was much more pleasant.

This isn't my usual veterinary clinic, but Dr. Chabanel has twice agreed to see my 13-year-old dog quickly.
He's a reassuring and competent doctor who explains each situation clearly.
I will definitely go to this clinic from now on.

Be very careful. Dont trust him. This man tells that a traitement or medicament doesnt exist while its not true. Im not silly and I decided to make an appointment at a real pets clinic to check and what a surprise - he told lie!
Thank you for the time you dedicated to my cat Freyja. Thank you for your care; thanks to you, I have a cat in excellent health again.
Never entrust your sick pet to this establishment; it risks death due to negligence.

I am posting this review to warn other pet owners.

My cat, Gribouille, was an extremely sweet, sociable, and trusting cat—a "dog-like cat," as this veterinarian himself described him.

He was treated for an ingrown claw on his paw pad. The procedure required anesthesia and a bandage extending up his leg.

What deeply shocked me was the way my cat's pain was treated, both during the treatment and when he woke up from anesthesia. When the bandage was removed, the Velcro was ripped off roughly, even though my cat was clearly in pain. When I asked why the bandage wasn't simply cut to avoid this pain, the procedure was continued without any consideration.

When my cat woke up from anesthesia, he was left without any real supervision, and we were asked to be more "firm," even rougher, to stimulate him, which broke my heart to see him treat my cat that way.

Furthermore, while this veterinarian himself mentioned the possibility of a heart problem, he prioritized extensive tests, including a biopsy, to look for cancer. Given the anesthetic risks in an animal with a potential heart condition, it seemed incomprehensible to me that a cardiac examination wasn't considered first. The anesthesia would very likely have killed him, as the veterinarian who took over his care clearly explained to me later.

Fortunately, I consulted another veterinarian, much more attentive, compassionate, and medically rigorous, who first assessed Gribouille's heart condition before making any invasive decisions. Thanks to this more careful and respectful approach, my cat was able to live another six months in good health.

I am leaving this review not out of resentment, but because gentle handling, rigorous assessment of anesthetic risks, and respect for animal pain are essential. These elements should be at the heart of all veterinary practice.
A trusted veterinary clinic. That's important for both animals and humans. A passionate veterinarian who always takes the time. A caring assistant—in short, a sure thing.
Attentive and understanding despite our delay, the clinic did the x-ray for our cat and we went home reassured. Thank you very much for our kitty.
Very unpleasant on the phone

I've been seeing Dr. Chabanel for my cats for several years now. Whether it's a simple booster vaccination or more complex procedures (teeth cleaning, stitches, tooth extractions, etc.), I've always been reassured by his honesty, professionalism, and above all, the care he gives to the animals. This veterinarian doesn't push unnecessary purchases or procedures to make money: you can tell he practices this profession out of love for life, not to get rich. His assistant is also very kind and reassuring!

Of all the veterinary clinics where I've taken my cats, this one is by far the best in every way! While Dr. Chabanel is certainly outspoken, he always remains courteous, smiling, and honest, and above all, gentle with the animals. In the end, he's not a smooth-talking salesman, but a truly excellent veterinarian.
He's completely untrustworthy, unpleasant, and I have no idea where he got his degree. I'd be terrified to take my dog ​​there. Run!
When I get another pet, I certainly won't entrust it to that overconfident vet.

A veterinarian who was able to establish an excellent rapport with my dog, despite her timid nature. The care he provided was highly effective; she was fully recovered in less than a week. His assistant is also very gentle and attentive to the owners' needs. I highly recommend this practice for their professionalism and availability.

Thinking I was calling my mother's vet in Gap for one of her cats, I ended up on this man. Yes, to err is human, and in my haste, I made a mistake. My God, what a mistake!

I was dealt with a condescending, aggressive, and rushed person, far from the kindness we expect from a veterinarian. After practically insulting me for calling the wrong clinic (even though I apologized), this gentleman hung up on me, saying, "That's enough, you're a pain!"

No further comment is needed...

As a cat owner myself, living in the Lyon area, I will never entrust my pet to your care! Your behavior is outrageous. Re-evaluate yourself, and if you're tired of this profession, consider a career change!

A word to the wise!
A professional veterinarian who loves animals. I recommend him.

The veterinarian and his assistant are very professional. This gentleman knows what he's doing and he does it very well... the animals and their owners appreciate it. My visit to this clinic was a huge relief. Thank you very much.

A very dedicated veterinarian who diagnoses illnesses like Sherlock Holmes. His receptionist is wonderful, very kind and always available. After trying several vets, this is by far my favorite practice! Your pet is in good hands.

It's clear Dr. Chabanel is a true animal lover. He saw me in an emergency for my cat, and I'm so grateful. He's also very patient. I went back to see him twice after my initial visit because I was so stressed. I'm so grateful for his patience. He's the best. His assistant is also wonderful, both kind and patient. I highly recommend this veterinarian.

This vet is aggressive and impatient with animals. He conducts consultations in the waiting room to maximize the number of clients he sees each day, and his training advice is straight out of the Middle Ages, riddled with outdated ideas about canine behavior. My dog ​​was very small when I first took him in. I went back two or three times for vaccinations and checkups, but I quickly stopped. I had to teach him not to be afraid of vets all over again. It was a disaster; avoid this place at all costs!
